payload.name: Preserve candidate facts when merging memories
payload.description: When constructing or updating memories, if a candidate describes a new distinct activity or event and you plan to MERGE it into existing memory, verify the merged memory retains all candidate key facts before committing.
content: Before applying MERGE to an existing memory, verify that the resulting content explicitly states every distinct fact from the candidate, especially the new activity/event, with its what, where, and when. Updating only a summary label while the body retains old details is insufficient.

If the candidate's distinct fact cannot be included without creating an unrelated or overloaded memory, do not MERGE; ADD a separate memory for the new activity/event or UPDATE a memory that supports it. Never let a merge erase the candidate's central information.

solves: During decision, a MERGE can drop a candidate's key fact when the existing memory covers an overlapping but different topic and the old body text is retained unchanged. This applies to any future construction decision in which a new distinct class, group, course, or event candidate is merged into a broader existing memory; it requires checking the post-merge text for candidate coverage and choosing ADD or a targeted UPDATE if the merge would lose that information.
